thread:
Sophia Nguyen: kicking off EU canary at T-0+5 for release v3.4.1 (commit 9f2a1b7). Need quick ack on fallback/runbook links. change window 10:00-12:00 PST.
Deploy Bot: canary rollout started -> target: 5% traffic to cluster eu-prod-canary, image: registry.redwood/v3.4.1@sha256:9f2a1b7. Canary ID: cb-3519876543.
Mike Patel: ack. what's our abort criteria?
Ravi Shah: primary thresholds: error-rate > 1.5% OR p95 latency increase > 200ms sustained over 5m -> abort canary and pin previous stable. Also if user-facing quality regressions reported by QA.
Sophia Nguyen: adding runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/rapid-fallback-opsplaybook (TL;DR steps below).
Jess Romero: release notes posted: https://docs.redwood.ai/releases/v3.4.1 — note: no DB schema changes, feature flags: new_cache_key opt-in.
Cameron Li: confirm no migration lock? DB read-only window NOT needed?
Ravi Shah: correct, no migrations. fallback is purely routing/model swap.
Sophia Nguyen: quick ops checklist excerpt:
```
1) Monitor cb-3519876543 in deploy dashboard
2) If threshold hit -> gretel rollback path
3) Pin previous: POST /api/admin/versions/pin {"service":"model-serving","version":"v3.4.0"}
4) Abort canary via deploy-bot: `/deploy abort cb-3519876543 --force`
5) If abort fails, run emergency k8s command on eu-prod control plane:
   kubectl -n model-svc patch svc model-router -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"v3.4.0"}}}'
6) Re-route traffic to fallback model: set route weight to 0 for canary
```

Mike Patel: small nit — add diagnostic steps before abort: capture flamegraphs and rolling logs: `curl https://ops.redwood/diag?canary=cb-3519876543` and `kubectl logs -n model-svc -l canary=cb-3519876543 --since=10m`
Sophia Nguyen: good call — added.
Deploy Bot: ALERT: cb-3519876543 healthcheck degraded -> 3 failed probes in 90s. Current canary weight 5%.
Ravi Shah: lowering weight to 1% now. `/deploy adjust cb-3519876543 --weight 1`
Deploy Bot: cb-3519876543 weight set to 1%.
Jess Romero: QA is seeing tokenization edge-case in output for a small corpus — logging a ticket (#INC-5921). If that escalates to user impact, escalate to rollback.
Cameron Li: oncall: any network flakiness in eu region?
Oncall Bot: incident feed: eu-az2 packet loss spike 10:07-10:11 UTC, mitigated. See https://status.redwood.internal/incident/2026-03-eu-az2
Mike Patel: since infra noisy, propose hold and let canary run at 0-1% for 10m, then decide. If we see steady errors revert.
Sophia Nguyen: agreed. I will be on standby. If we need manual rollback, use this emergency CLI sequence (in order):
```
# 1. Abort via deploy-bot
/deploy abort cb-3519876543 --reason "healthcheck regression"
# 2. Pin previous stable
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"service":"model-serving","version":"v3.4.0"}' https://api.redwood.internal/admin/versions/pin
# 3. Force traffic route to stable
kubectl -n model-svc patch svc model-router -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"v3.4.0"}}}'
# 4. Clear canary KV cache if serving stale prefixes
curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.internal/cache/clear -d '{"scope":"canary","id":"cb-3519876543"}'
```

Ravi Shah: also add a post-rollback smoke: run `npm run smoke:eu` and check endpoints `/v1/health` and `/v1/generate` for latency and sample outputs.
Jess Romero: I'll prepare a one-paragraph customer-facing blurb if we end up rolling back.
Sophia Nguyen: thanks all. leaving the canary at 1% for 10m. if no further degradation by 10:25 UTC we can either ramp to 10% or cut. Will post final decision here. :eyes:
Deploy Bot: note: runbook rapid-fallback updated by Sophia Nguyen at 10:12 UTC -> https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/rapid-fallback-opsplaybook?updated=true
Sophia Nguyen: final: holding. will escalate if thresholds crossed. ping me directly if you see anything urgent.
Mike Patel: ACK. :thumbsup:
Ravi Shah: ACK.
Jess Romero: ACK.
Cameron Li: ACK.
Oncall Bot: scheduled reminder in 10m for decision checkpoint.
